  RESOLUTION NO.
 4
  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION OF
 5  THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
 6  CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR KRISTEN ROBERTS
  REPRESENTING RAISING CANE’S CHICKEN FINGERS TO
 7  ALLOW 1) NEW CONSTRUCTIONS WITH A VALUATION THAT
  EXCEED TWENTY THOUSAND DOLLARS ($20,000.00) AND 2)
 8  OUTDOOR DINING WITHIN A NEW APPROXIMATELY 6,300
 9  SQUARE-FOOT TWO-STORY FAST FOOD RESTAURANT
  WITH A DRIVE THROUGH ON AN APPROXIMATELY 55,200
10  SQUARE-FOOT C-2 (GENERAL COMMERCIAL )/MEDICAL
  ENTERPRISE OVERLAY ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT
11  401 SOUTH PRAIRIE AVENUE
12
  (CASE NO. SP- 2021-005)
13
  SECTION 1.
14
  Pursuant to Chapter 12, Articles 5.1, 7 and 25 of the Inglewood Municipal
15
  Code, there was filed with the Planning Commission of the City of Inglewood,
16
  California on the fifth day of April 2021, an application by Kristen Roberts
17
  representing Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers for a Special Use Permit request to
18
  allow 1) new construction with a valuation that exceeds twenty thousand dollars
19
  ($20,000.00) and 2) outdoor dining within a new approximately 6,300 square-foot
20
  two-story fast food restaurant with a drive-through on an approximately 55,200
21
  square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial)/Medical Enterprise Overlay zoned property
22
  legally described as:
23
  Lots 5 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of Block 4 of Tract No. 446
24
  (AIN 4021-036-027 and 049)
25
  The application was set for a public hearing before the Planning Commission in the
26
  City Council Chambers, Ninth Floor of City Hall, on the fifth day of May 2021,
27
  beginning at the hour of 7:00 p.m., and;
28
  Notice of the time was given as required by law, and;

  1
   Planning Commission Meeting-May 5, 2021
  ITEM 5b-Revised Resolution (Final Draft)
 1
 2
  The Commission conducted the hearing at the time stated in the notice and
 3
  afforded all persons interested in the matter of the Special Use Permit, or in any
 4
  matter or subject related thereto, an opportunity to address the Commission and be
 5
  heard and to submit any testimony or evidence in favor of or against the granting of
 6
  the Special Use Permit.
 7
  SECTION 2.
 8
  The Planning Commission has carefully considered all testimony and
 9
  evidence presented at the hearing and now finds as follows:
10
  1.  That the site is adequate in size and shape to accommodate the structure
11
  with a valuation that exceeds twenty thousand dollars ($20,000.00) and the
12
  proposed outdoor dining areas in a proposed two-story fast food restaurant
13
  because the development will meet the minimum parking requirements in
14
  compliance with the IMC and provides adequate space for site ingress and
15
  egress.
16
  2.  The site is adequately served by streets of appropriate width and function
17
  to carry the kind of traffic to be generated by the structure with a valuation
18
  that exceeds twenty thousand dollars ($20,000.00) and the outdoor dining
19
  areas in a proposed two-story fast food restaurant because the required
20
  parking for the development will be provided on-site and accessed along
21
  Prairie Avenue and Manchester Boulevard.
22
  3.  That this application is in compliance with the provisions of Chapter 12,
23
  Articles 5.1, 7, and 25 of the Inglewood Municipal Code because the
24
  structure with a valuation that exceeds twenty thousand dollars
25
  ($20,000.00) and the proposed outdoor dining areas in a proposed two-
26
  story fast food restaurant are allowed by the IMC, subject to Special Use
27
  Permit approval.
28

  2
   Planning Commission Meeting-May 5, 2021
  ITEM 5b-Revised Resolution (Final Draft)
 1
 2
  4.  The granting of the Special Use Permit for the structure with a valuation that
 3
  exceeds twenty thousand dollars ($20,000.00) and the proposed outdoor
 4
  dining areas in a proposed two-story fast food restaurant will not be
 5
  detrimental to properties in the immediate neighborhood and will not have a
 6
  negative effect on the public safety or general welfare of the community
 7
  because it will not affect existing circulation or development patterns or land
 8
  uses.
 9
  5.  That the proposed structure with a valuation that exceeds twenty thousand
10
  dollars ($20,000.00) and the outdoor dining areas in a proposed two-story
11
  fast food restaurant conforms to the guidelines of the Commercial Residential
12
  land use designation in that it:
13
    Creates and maintains a healthy economic condition within the
14
  present business community;
15
    Assist new businesses to locate within the city and it ensures the
16
  availability of services for the needs of the residents in the
17
  community.
18
  6.  That this project is categorically exempt from the requirements of the
19
  California Environmental Quality Act, pursuant to Notice of Exemption (EA-
20
  CE-2021-035).
21
  SECTION 3.
22
  NOW, THEREFORE, THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
23
  INGLEWOOD , CALIFORNIA , DOES HEREBY RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:
24
  That Special Use Permit No. 2021-005 is hereby granted subject to the
25
  following conditions and limitations:
26
  1.  That the applicant adheres to all applicable provisions of the Inglewood
27
  Municipal Code as well as County, State and Federal laws.
28

  3
   Planning Commission Meeting-May 5, 2021
  ITEM 5b-Revised Resolution (Final Draft)
 1
 2
  2.  That the applicant shall obtain Site Plan Review approval from Planning
 3
  Division, any other  required permits from the Building Safety Division,
 4
  Public Works Department, Los Angeles County Fire Department, and
 5
  other City departments as applicable.
 6
  3.  That the hours of operation for the restaurant and drive-thru shall be from
 7
  9:00 AM to 3:30 AM, seven days a week.
 8
  4.  That the applicant shall install and maintain a minimum of seven exterior
 9
  and 16 interior security cameras of the tenant space. The precise number
10
  and location of said cameras to be determined during Site Plan Review.
11
  Said cameras must be capable of producing a retrievable image that can be
12
  made a permanent record and that can be enlarged through projection or
13
  other means. Cameras meeting the requirements of this section shall be
14
  maintained in proper working order at all times and shall be subject to
15
  periodic inspection by the Inglewood Police Department.
16
  5.  That the applicant must provide “outside expo process” (line-busting) at the
17
  subject site when the drive-thru queuing lane exceeds ten (10) cars per lane
18
  by deploying Crewmembers standing outside the drive-thru pickup window
19
  expediting orders to cars.
20
  6.  That the applicant must provide for contactless ordering by providing a
21
  mobile online ordering system and any other means required by the Los
22
  Angeles County Department of Public Health.
23
  7.  That an anti-graffiti finish shall be utilized on all exposed walls under 10
24
  feet as determined by the Planning Division.
25
  8.  That the applicant shall power wash the entire property twice a month and
26
  comply with all National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES)
27
  requirements.
28

  4
   Planning Commission Meeting-May 5, 2021
  ITEM 5b-Revised Resolution (Final Draft)
 1
 2
  9.  That the applicant shall provide to the Planning Division, Code-Enforcement
 3
  Division, and Traffic Division the name, telephone number, fax number, and
 4
  email address of a contact person responsible for on-site circulation and
 5
  related off-site traffic management.
 6
  10.  That the applicant shall develop and operate in compliance with an
 7
  ingress/egress traffic circulation, queuing management and operations plan
 8
  (addressing both special event periods and non-special event periods) to be
 9
  reviewed and approved by the Traffic Division of the Public Works
10
  Department (Traffic Division). This plan shall be designed to prevent the
11
  potential for vehicle queues to spill onto surrounding public Right-of-Ways
12
  and shall include enforcement mechanisms that the City can employ to
13
  ensure ongoing compliance. Said plan shall be submitted to the City for
14
  review prior to issuance of a Building Permit for new construction. The plan
15
  must be approved by the Traffic Division prior to issuance of a Certificate of
16
  Occupancy.
17
  11.  As part of the required parcel map process, the applicant shall work
18
  cooperatively with the City on land dedications for both 1) the creation of
19
  wider sidewalks on Manchester Boulevard and Prairie Avenue as well as 2)
20
  a dedicated right turn lane on eastbound Manchester Boulevard and/or a
21
  dedicated right turn lane on southbound Prairie Avenue, with dimension
22
  requirements to be determined by the Traffic Division of the Public Works
23
  Department.
24
  12.  That the management personnel of the business shall be responsible for
25
  continuously supervising and maintaining both the interior and exterior of
26
  the premises in terms of noise, patron behavior, loitering and related
27
  activities. The management personnel shall be responsible for the continual
28
  removal of litter from the premises and for the removal from neighboring

  5
   Planning Commission Meeting-May 5, 2021
  ITEM 5b-Revised Resolution (Final Draft)
 1
 2
  properties of littered objects initially purchased from the subject fast food
 3
  restaurant.
 4
  13.  That the applicant shall provide the name, telephone number, fax number,
 5
  and email address of a contact person responsible for the maintenance of
 6
  the building to the Planning Division and update the information within 30
 7
  days of change of ownership of the property to ensure continuous
 8
  maintenance of the subject property.
 9
  14.  That all improvements to the property will be continuously maintained,
10
  including but not limited to repairs to the structures and replacement of
11
  dead or diseased plants.
12
  15.  That the applicant must install a no left turn sign on the northwest corner of
13
  the two-way driveway abutting Manchester Boulevard.
14
  16.  That the Parcel Map must comply with the subdivision map act and that prior
15
  to issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy the applicant must record the
16
  Parcel Map with the Los Angeles County Recorder’s office and City’s Public
17
  Works Department.
18
  17.  That the granting of this Special Use Permit is contingent upon the further
19
  limitation that the Special Use Permit is not valid until all conditions have
20
  been complied with. Failure to comply with any of these conditions shall be
21
  cause for revocation of this Special Use Permit.
22
  18.  That this Special Use Permit shall become null and void if not utilized within
23
  one (1) year of the effective date hereof subject to any extensions approved
24
  by the Planning Commission. For purposes of this Special Use Permit
25
  “utilized” means the applicant has applied for Site Plan Review and
26
  recorded the covenant.
27
  19.  That this resolution shall be recorded with the Los Angeles County
28
  Recorder’s office prior to final plan approval being issued by the Planning

 7
  information.
